## Description

Primary source:

<https://ngs101.com/how-to-analyze-single-cell-rna-seq-data-complete-beginners-guide-part-7-2-trajectory-analysis-using-slingshot/>

Part 2 of 3. Slingshot is run on the T/NK `SingleCellExperiment` from part 1,
using the UMAP embedding and Seurat clusters. The result is a set of
**lineages** (ordered paths through clusters), one **principal curve** per
lineage, a **pseudotime** per cell per lineage (`NA` for cells not on a lineage),
and **weights** (how strongly each cell belongs to each lineage).

Each lineage has its own pseudotime scale. A single "consensus" pseudotime per
cell is built here from the lineage with the highest weight (the article's
"Strategy 1"); because the lineages share a trunk but have different lengths,
this single value is a convenience for plotting and correlation, not an exact
common clock.

Code is taken from the source article's code blocks (steps 7-10). Changes made
for this notebook series: hard-coded values moved into the YAML front matter,
paths built from `params` rather than `setwd()`, and changes marked `ADDED:` or
`FIX:` in comments.

## Libraries and directories

```{r step1_libs_data}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: Load required libraries
#-----------------------------------------------

# Core trajectory analysis
library(slingshot)
library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(princurve)
library(TrajectoryUtils)

# Single-cell analysis infrastructure
library(Seurat)
library(SeuratObject)

# Data manipulation
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Visualization
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(viridis)
library(scales)
library(grDevices)

if (!exists("params") || !is.list(params)) {
  # Running interactively (e.g. via "Run Cell") rather than through
  # knit/render, so `params` was never created by rmarkdown::render().
  # Reconstruct it by parsing this .Rmd's own YAML header, so the params
  # defaults live in exactly one place (the YAML block above) instead of
  # being duplicated here.
  rmd_path <- tryCatch(
    # Only reliable when this document is the active editor tab; if focus
    # has moved to another file, this will pick up the wrong path.
    rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path,
    error = function(e) NA_character_
  )
  if (is.na(rmd_path) || !nzchar(rmd_path)) {
    # Fallback if rstudioapi is unavailable or no doc is focused; assumes
    # the working directory is the project root.
    rmd_path <- "scRNAseq_tutorial_7-2_trajectory_slingshot/tut7-2_trajectory_slingshot_part2.Rmd"
  }
  params <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(rmd_path)$params
}

# Set working directory
base.dir <- params$base.dir
traj.dir <- file.path(base.dir, params$traj.subdir)

# Create organized output directories
for (d in c("plots/trajectories", "plots/pseudotime", "results")) {
  if (!dir.exists(file.path(traj.dir, d))) dir.create(file.path(traj.dir, d), recursive = TRUE)
}

# Set random seed for reproducibility
set.seed(params$seed)

# Configure plotting defaults
theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = 12))

# Column names from params
celltype.col <- params$celltype.col
cluster.col <- params$cluster.col
condition.col <- params$condition.col
```

```{r step2_load_obj}
# ADDED: hand-off from part 1
sce <- readRDS(file.path(traj.dir, "results/sce_T_NK.rds"))

    paste(reducedDimNames(sce), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
```

## Run Slingshot trajectory inference on the T/NK lineage

```{r step3_slingshot}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 7: Run Slingshot trajectory inference on T/NK lineage
#-----------------------------------------------

# First, examine cluster composition to identify start cluster
cat("Cluster composition in T/NK lineage:\n")
cluster_celltype_table <- table(colData(sce)[[cluster.col]], colData(sce)[[celltype.col]])
print(cluster_celltype_table)
cat("\n")

# Identify cluster(s) enriched for CD4+ T cells (likely contains naive populations)
stopifnot(params$start.celltype %in% colnames(cluster_celltype_table))
cd4_per_cluster <- cluster_celltype_table[, params$start.celltype]
cd4_enriched_clusters <- names(cd4_per_cluster)[cd4_per_cluster > params$start.min_cells]

cat("Clusters enriched for ", params$start.celltype, " (>", params$start.min_cells, " cells):\n", sep = "")
print(cd4_enriched_clusters)
cat("\n")

# For this tutorial, we'll let Slingshot auto-detect OR you can manually specify
# If you want manual control, set params$sling.start_clus to a CD4+ enriched cluster
# NOTE: the article's own printed result auto-detects a start at cluster 8,
# which is a CD8+ T cell cluster, not one of the CD4+ enriched clusters above
start.clus <- if (nzchar(params$sling.start_clus)) params$sling.start_clus else NULL
end.clus <- if (nzchar(params$sling.end_clus)) trimws(strsplit(params$sling.end_clus, ",")[[1]]) else NULL

cat("Running Slingshot trajectory inference...\n")
cat("  Using: UMAP coordinates\n")
cat("  Clustering: Seurat clusters\n")
cat("  Start:", if (is.null(start.clus)) "Auto-detect (or manually specify CD4+ T cell cluster)" else start.clus, "\n")
cat("  End:", if (is.null(end.clus)) "Auto-detect (likely NK cell clusters)" else paste(end.clus, collapse = ", "), "\n\n")

# Run Slingshot
sce <- slingshot(
  sce,
  clusterLabels = cluster.col,         # Use Seurat cluster assignments
  reducedDim = "UMAP",                 # Use UMAP coordinates
  start.clus = start.clus,             # Auto-detect OR specify cluster number
  end.clus = end.clus,                 # Auto-detect terminal clusters
  allow.breaks = params$sling.allow_breaks, # Don't allow gaps in lineages
  extend = params$sling.extend,        # Don't extend curves beyond data
  reweight = params$sling.reweight,    # Refit curves after initial fit
  reassign = params$sling.reassign     # Reassign cells to best-fit curves
)

cat("Slingshot trajectory inference complete!\n\n")

# Quick validation: Check if trajectory makes biological sense
lineages <- slingLineages(sce)
cat("Number of lineages detected:", length(lineages), "\n")

for (i in seq_along(lineages)) {
  cat("Lineage", i, ":", paste(lineages[[i]], collapse = " → "), "\n")
}
```

## Lineages, principal curves and pseudotime

```{r step4_extract}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 8: Extract and examine Slingshot results for T/NK lineage
#-----------------------------------------------

# Extract lineages (cluster-level trajectories)
lineages <- slingLineages(sce)

cat("=== Slingshot Lineages for T/NK Cells ===\n")
cat("Number of lineages detected:", length(lineages), "\n\n")

for (i in seq_along(lineages)) {
  cat("Lineage", i, ":", paste(lineages[[i]], collapse = " → "), "\n")
}
cat("\n")

# Extract curves (cell-level fitted principal curves)
curves <- slingCurves(sce)
cat("Number of principal curves fit:", length(curves), "\n\n")

# Extract pseudotime (one column per lineage)
pseudotime_matrix <- slingPseudotime(sce)
cat("Pseudotime matrix dimensions:", dim(pseudotime_matrix), "\n")
cat("  (Rows = cells, Columns = lineages)\n\n")

# Extract cell weights (probability of belonging to each lineage)
curve_weights <- slingCurveWeights(sce)
cat("Cell weights dimensions:", dim(curve_weights), "\n")
cat("  (Rows = cells, Columns = lineages)\n")
cat("  Weight = probability cell belongs to lineage\n\n")

# Summary statistics per lineage
for (i in seq_along(lineages)) {
  pt <- pseudotime_matrix[, i]
  cat("Lineage", i, "pseudotime:\n")
  cat("  Range:", round(range(pt, na.rm = TRUE), 2), "\n")
  cat("  Cells assigned:", sum(!is.na(pt)), "\n")
  cat("  Median:", round(median(pt, na.rm = TRUE), 2), "\n\n")
}
```

## Create consensus pseudotime for T/NK cells

```{r step5_consensus}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 9: Create consensus pseudotime for T/NK cells
#-----------------------------------------------

# Strategy 1: Use primary lineage (highest weight)
primary_lineage <- apply(curve_weights, 1, which.max)
sce$primary_lineage <- paste0("Lineage_", primary_lineage)

# Extract pseudotime from primary lineage for each cell
sce$slingshot_pseudotime <- sapply(1:ncol(sce), function(i) {
  lineage <- primary_lineage[i]
  pseudotime_matrix[i, lineage]
})

cat("Primary pseudotime assignment for T/NK cells:\n")
cat("  Cells per lineage:\n")
print(table(sce$primary_lineage))
cat("\n")

cat("Pseudotime summary (primary lineage method):\n")
cat("  Range:", round(range(sce$slingshot_pseudotime, na.rm = TRUE), 2), "\n")
cat("  Median:", round(median(sce$slingshot_pseudotime, na.rm = TRUE), 2), "\n\n")

# Pseudotime by cell type
pseudotime_by_type <- data.frame(
  pseudotime = sce$slingshot_pseudotime,
  cell_type = colData(sce)[[celltype.col]],
  lineage = sce$primary_lineage,
  condition = colData(sce)[[condition.col]]
)

cat("Median pseudotime by cell type (T/NK lineage):\n")
summary_stats <- pseudotime_by_type %>%
  group_by(cell_type) %>%
  summarise(
    median_pt = median(pseudotime, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_pt = mean(pseudotime, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_cells = n()
  ) %>%
  arrange(median_pt)

print(as.data.frame(summary_stats))
```

## Visualize T/NK trajectories

```{r step6_visualize, fig.width = 16, fig.height = 12}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 10: Visualize Slingshot trajectories for T/NK lineage
#-----------------------------------------------

# Extract UMAP coordinates and trajectory data
umap_df <- data.frame(
  UMAP1 = reducedDim(sce, "UMAP")[, 1],
  UMAP2 = reducedDim(sce, "UMAP")[, 2],
  pseudotime = sce$slingshot_pseudotime,
  cell_type = colData(sce)[[celltype.col]],
  condition = colData(sce)[[condition.col]],
  cluster = colData(sce)[[cluster.col]],
  lineage = sce$primary_lineage
)

# Plot 1: Slingshot curves on T/NK cells
curves.png <- file.path(traj.dir, "plots/trajectories/02_slingshot_T_NK_curves.png")
png(curves.png,
    width = 10, height = 8, units = "in", res = params$plot.dpi)

plot(reducedDim(sce, "UMAP"),
     col = scales::alpha(as.numeric(factor(colData(sce)[[celltype.col]])), 0.5),
     pch = 16, cex = 0.5,
     xlab = "UMAP 1", ylab = "UMAP 2",
     main = "Slingshot Trajectory: T/NK Cell Lineage")

lines(SlingshotDataSet(sce), lwd = 3, col = "black", type = "lineages")

legend("topright",
       legend = levels(factor(colData(sce)[[celltype.col]])),
       col = 1:length(levels(factor(colData(sce)[[celltype.col]]))),
       pch = 16, cex = 0.8, bty = "n")

dev.off()

# Plot 2: Pseudotime gradient
p_pseudotime <- ggplot(umap_df, aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2, color = pseudotime)) +
  geom_point(size = 1, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_viridis(option = "plasma", name = "Pseudotime") +
  labs(title = "T/NK Lineage: Slingshot Pseudotime",
       x = "UMAP 1", y = "UMAP 2") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))

# Plot 3: Cell types
p_celltype <- ggplot(umap_df, aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2, color = cell_type)) +
  geom_point(size = 1, alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "T/NK Cell Types",
       x = "UMAP 1", y = "UMAP 2") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))

# Plot 4: Lineage assignment
p_lineage <- ggplot(umap_df, aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2, color = lineage)) +
  geom_point(size = 1, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(title = "Lineage Assignment",
       x = "UMAP 1", y = "UMAP 2") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))

# Combine plots
p_overview <- (p_pseudotime | p_celltype) / (p_lineage | plot_spacer())
print(p_overview)

ggsave(file.path(traj.dir, "plots/trajectories/03_slingshot_T_NK_overview.png"),
       p_overview, width = 16, height = 12, dpi = params$plot.dpi)

# Violin plot
p_violin <- ggplot(umap_df, aes(x = reorder(cell_type, pseudotime, median),
                                 y = pseudotime, fill = cell_type)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, fill = "white", outlier.shape = NA) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Pseudotime Distribution by Cell Type (T/NK Lineage)",
       x = "Cell Type", y = "Pseudotime") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
print(p_violin)

ggsave(file.path(traj.dir, "plots/pseudotime/04_pseudotime_by_celltype_T_NK.png"),
       p_violin, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = params$plot.dpi)
```
